name: 2018 Pikachu Project
description:
Pokémon the Movie: The Power of Us (Japanese: ポケットモンスター　みんなの the Movie: Everyone's Story; officially known as Pokémon the Movie: Everyone's Story in Japan) is the twenty-first Pokémon movie, and the second released during the broadcast of Pokémon the Series: Sun & Moon.

It was released in Japan on July 13, 2018, and received a limited release in the United Kingdom, Ireland, United States, and Canada starting on November 24, 2018, in Australia and New Zealand starting on November 25, 2018, and in the Philippines starting on December 5, 2018. The English dub was first screened in Singapore on November 12, 2018, followed by a release in Singaporean theaters beginning November 15, 2018. It premiered on Pokémon in the United States on December 8, 2018.

It was first revealed in a teaser trailer that aired on Oha Suta in Japan on December 10, 2017. A full trailer was later released on February 27, 2018. A new trailer was released on April 9, 2018, officially revealing Zeraora to have a role in the film.

It is the second movie of a trilogy set in an alternate continuity from the main series established in I Choose You!, and is followed by Secrets of the Jungle and Distant Blue Sky!.

name: 5ban Graphics
description:
5ban Graphics is a group of artists within Creatures, Inc. who have illustrated many cards for the Pokémon Trading Card Game from Black & White onward. The group has designed many Trainer Cards, as well as many Full Art cards and Pokémon cards for the Black and White, XY, Sun & Moon, Sword & Shield, and Scarlet & Violet TCG Series. 

In 2012, a brief interview about the creation of card artwork was posted on the Creatures, Inc. PTCG blog in which they state they like to make the Pokémon look 3D along with exemplifying the best qualities of the Pokémon when possible so they stand out on their own. The group's name is a reference to Creatures' former address at 10 Gobancho, Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo.

name: AKIRA EGAWA
description:
AKIRA EGAWA (Japanese: あきら Egawa Akira) is a freelance illustrator who has worked on the Pokémon series. She began illustrating cards in 2019 for the Pokémon Trading Card Game with Riolu (Unified Minds 115), included in the Unified Minds expansion. She has also illustrated for Pokémon Masters EX, providing artwork for the Dreams of the Void event.

In addition to being an illustrator for cards themselves, EGAWA also illustrated booster pack artwork for the international releases of the Battle Styles, Chilling Reign, Evolving Skies, and Fusion Strike expansions. She was among the panel of judges for the Illustration contests.

EGAWA's art style focuses on giving the subject detailed textures, with the goal of making them look "cool". She has previous experience with 3D modelling, but she currently primarily creates illustrations by painting in Photoshop. Credits outside Pokémon include other mobile and card games such as , and , and the Card Game.

EGAWA has been playing the Pokémon games since Generation II.

name: Amelicart
description:
Amelicart (Japanese: ア・メリカ) is a Tokyo-based freelance illustrator who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Amelicart was a participant in the Illustration contests, where his submitted artwork of Slowpoke won the Slowpoke Award. The Slowpoke Award was not originally a part of the contest, but was given out due to the piece's popularity among the panel of judges.

Amelicart's first official art for the Pokémon franchise was for the "GOOD GOOD SMILE!" line of Pokémon Center merchandise. Amelicart would begin illustrating official cards with the Crown Zenith expansion, where he illustrated Bibarel (Crown Zenith GG25) and a small collection of staple Item cards: Lost Vacuum (Crown Zenith 135), Rescue Carrier (Crown Zenith 142), Trekking Shoes (Crown Zenith 145), and Ultra Ball (Crown Zenith 146).

Amelicart produces his lineless artwork with PhotoShop. He works as a guest professor at the Kyoto University of the Arts, and his other credits include , , and the Hobonichi Project.

name: Asako Ito
description:
Asako Ito (Japanese: いとうあさこ Itō Asako, born in Miyagi Prefecture) is an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Her first card was Poliwag (Sun & Moon 30) from the Sun & Moon expansion. 

She is unique among TCG artists as, rather than drawing or making a 3D render, she crochets stuffed dolls of the subject. She also crafts the backgrounds for her card artworks using various materials such as felt. She taught herself knitting at university, although she had majored in oil painting. According to her, she was inspired to learn to knit after seeing the teddy bear from the series and wanting to knit a replica for herself.

name: Asuka Iwashita
description:
Asuka Iwashita (Japanese: ) is a conceptual character artist for PTS, specifically the sixth, seventh, and twelfth Pokémon movies. In addition to these three movies, she worked on the special episode The Mastermind of Mirage Pokémon.

In addition to working on Pokémon the Series, Iwashita worked as a graphic designer for multiple Pokémon games from Gold and Silver through Emerald. In addition to being a designer for the games' graphics, she is also credited for designing Pokémon in Generation III.

Her first illustrations were featured in Pokémon VS, in which she illustrated all of Sabrina's featured Pokémon. In 2004, three years after illustrating these cards, she was credited as an illustrator for the last time on Makuhita (EX Deoxys 65).

name: Atsuko Nishida
description:
Atsuko Nishida (Japanese: 西田敦子 / にしだあつこ Nishida Atsuko) is a graphic artist who has been involved with several aspects of the Pokémon franchise since it began. She was part of the graphics team on Pulseman, one of Game Freak's most successful early titles, working alongside Pokémon creator Satoshi Tajiri and artist Ken Sugimori. During the development of the first Pokémon games, she helped design key characters and several Pokémon, notably the cuter ones as opposed to the tougher ones.

Nishida is a character designer for the mascot of the Pokémon franchise, Pikachu. She stated that first design of Pikachu looked like a vertically long daifuku rice confection with ears. She also modeled Pikachu's cheeks, which are used to store electricity, after squirrels storing food in their cheeks. Nishida is also a fan of Eevee and the Eeveelutions, having personally designed almost all of the Eeveelutions, with the exception of Jolteon and Flareon. Nishida has continued to work within many areas of the franchise, credited on the majority of the core series games and movies, and has produced an array of original illustrations for the Pokémon Trading Card Game. She is also the illustrator for the mini-comic series titled Together with Pokémon! (Japanese: ポケモンといっしょ！) for a monthly children's magazine, Chara Pafe (Japanese: キャラぱふぇ).

Pikachu ex's Ascended Heroes print was booota's first card released in English.

During her absence from the TCG, booota also contributed bonus artwork for Project VOLTAGE.

name: Eske Yoshinob
description:
Eske Yoshinob is a freelance illustrator and programmer who has provided work for the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Originally a game model designer working for Now Production, he later moved on to producing 3D CG material for Daiichi Sankyo before becoming employed at Square Visual Works, part of Square Enix, in 2005. While there he was involved setup simulation, pipeline tool development, and model creation/animation for games in the Final Fantasy series and the Kingdom Hearts series. Concurrently, he also worked at Exit Tunes, Inc., then called Quake Holdings, as an illustrator, primarily involved in the production of album covers for the Exit Trance series. He chose to go freelance at the end of 2009.

In 2010, he provided 3D model and animation work while at Polygon Pictures, and was involved in the development of Transformers Prime and Tron: Uprising. He began producing illustrations for the Pokémon Trading Card Game in 2011, and began providing workflow and pipeline solutions for Toei Animation in 2012.

His first illustration was Sunkern (Neo Destiny 83), a card released in the Neo Destiny expansion in March 2001. He is also credited as the illustrator for all of Lt. Surge's Pokémon in the Pokémon VS expansion. Not only had Hattori worked for the Trading Card Game, but he had worked in Graphic Support for the Pokémon Channel spin-off game. He also created the artwork for the Pokémon Fossil Museum.

Framestore is a British visual effects studio that works on advertising, television, and film. The studio has won Academy Awards for its work on , , and .

Framestore worked on as a secondary studio in the art, animation, and visual effects departments. It is credited as an illustrator in the for certain cards associated with the film. Additionally, Framestore created the launch trailer for Sword and Shield.

name: Fujimoto Gold
description:
Fujimoto Gold (Japanese: フジモトゴールド Fujimoto Gold; born 1993) is an illustrator, concept artist and designer, living in Kobe Hyogo. Originally studying business administration, statistic and human resource management at a university in Kobe, he decided on becoming a freelance illustrator for a year. Whilst also working part-time in the restaurant industry, he became interested in manufacturing, leading him to enter the Graphic Design Department of the Kobe City College of Technology. His career as an illustrator began in full after this graduation, whilst he also worked as a web designer and coder at an IT company. His pen-name, "Fujimoto Gold", was a nickname given to him by the owner of a restaurant he worked under as a form of praise. Much of Fujimoto's early professional career was centered around promotional pieces for the city of Kobe.

Fujimoto's debut as staff on the Pokémon series was as the sole background artist on POKÉTOON's Snorunt's Summer Vacation. Just a year later, he'd enter the 2022 TCG Illustration Contest with art of Charizard, Greninja and Pikachu, though would not progress past the quarter-finals. In 2023, he was charged with the task of adapting the character designs from Detective Pikachu Returns to animation, as the character designer of Detective Pikachu & the Mystery of the Missing Flan. In 2024, he finally went on to produce official artwork for the Pokémon Trading Card Game, the first of which being Gastly (Temporal Forces 102) from the Temporal Forces expansion.

name: GAME FREAK inc.
description:
Game Freak, Inc. (Japanese: Game Freak), officially stylized as GAME FREAK inc. or less commonly as GAMEFREAK inc., is a Japanese game development company founded on April 26, 1989 by Satoshi Tajiri, Ken Sugimori, and Junichi Masuda. Game Freak is responsible for the development of the core series Pokémon games, the free-to-play spin-off game Quest, and as a co-developer of Pokopia, alongside Koei Tecmo and The Pokémon Company. The company shares ownership of The Pokémon Company with Creatures, Inc. and Nintendo.

The company has 249 employees as of March 2025, while Satoshi Tajiri serves as its Representative director (Japan). Its headquarters were initially located on the Kashiwa 3rd building in Shimokitazawa. It moved to Carrot Tower on November 19, 2007 and to Kanda Square in Nishikichō between May and July 2020.

Game Freak launched its website on January 29, 1997. Between October 1999 and November 1999, the head office address and phone numbers were removed. The address would then be readded during summer 2007.

On September 17, 2020, it was reported on Weibo that Game Freak trademarked its Chinese name as Game Maniac after changing it from Game Freak.

In Korean, the company is called Game Freak.

Game Freak acquired and absorbed the mobile development company Koa Games in October 2015.

name: Hajime Kusajima
description:
Hajime Kusajima (Japanese: 草嶋一) is an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Kusajima's first cards were Owner's Pokémon (TCG) from the Japanese Pokémon VS expansion. His first English cards released in the Expedition Base Set expansion.

Over the years, he has changed his style several times. During the e-Card Series, Kusajima's method consisted of watercolor and ink, but he also used varying intensities depending on the Pokémon portrayed. In some cases he used light tones with thin outlines, but for more dominant images, switched to deeper colors with heavier brushstrokes and thicker outlines. During the early EX Series, he switched to a more computer-aided style with solid colors and tone highlights that gave an almost cartoon-like appearance. It was also during this time that he began to use often very colorful or detailed backgrounds in order to create contrast. Towards the end of the EX Series, he expanded on this style by using much heavier outlines, larger areas of shadow and more vivid colors while also experimenting with his original style to produce soft and realistic images by effectively using light and shadow. He would not illustrate any other cards until the Stormfront expansion, where he again demonstrated the variety of his coloring techniques over the coming sets. Some featured plainly colored images and others with varying brushstroke effects, while some featured extremely deep colors and areas of shadow, as well as the complete opposite with images highlighted with intense light. Kusajima stopped contributing new artwork to the TCG around the beginning of the Sun & Moon Series.

name: HiRON
description:
Hirofumi Nakano (Japanese: 中野博文), born in Tokyo, is a 3D illustrator who has provided artwork for the Pokémon Trading Card Game on a few occasions, with his first appearing in the Dragons Exalted expansion. He is normally credited as "HiRON" (ハイロン) in his work.

Nakano is a member of DigitalImage, a part-time digital design lecturer at the Niigata College of Art & Design, and a part-time illustration lecturer at the Tokyo Designer Gakuin College. His work primarily features on covers and in articles of computing and car magazines. Subjects are often exaggerated versions of their normal counterparts, with vehicles such as cars and aircraft created to make them appear more futuristic, and anthropomorphized animals with proportionally larger body parts. Among his interests, he often delves into the realms of science fiction and animation for his work, with images including various types of mecha or assorted creatures. Many of his images are illuminated with an intense light and textured with a highly reflective surface. Nakano regularly participates in producing exhibition work, and has also branched into producing some of his work into jewelry, as well as creating traditional Japanese illustrations for smart phone cases and music players.

name: Hironobu Yoshida
description:
Hironobu Yoshida (Japanese: 吉田宏信; born 1972) is a graphic designer who has been involved with several aspects of the Pokémon franchise for many years. Since Yellow in 1997, Yoshida has had a hand in the development of the majority of core series Pokémon games, both as a graphic and Pokémon designer. 

He is credited in several of the Pokémon movies within the character design department and has illustrated a handful of cards for the Pokémon Trading Card Game. He also designed the main art for the World Championships since 2007. The Pokémon he is known to have designed include Wobbuffet, Dunsparce, and several Legendary and Mythical Pokémon such as Celebi, Rayquaza, Deoxys, and Darkrai.

Additionally, he created an array of unique characters and lent his voice to some of them for the Game Boy Advance game Drill Dozer, another Game Freak title directed by fellow Pokémon designer Ken Sugimori in 2005.

He has also branched into other media, performing a live-action version of the Poké Dude Show (an in-game tutorial featured in FireRed and LeafGreen), dressing up as Primo, the Poké Dude, and giving advice on how to do various things in the Pokémon games. He reprises this role in the song Teach Me, Poké Dude!, in which he engages a group of children in the same manner as the in-game character and provides the main vocals.

name: Hitoshi Ariga
description:
Hitoshi Ariga (Japanese: 有賀 ヒトシ Ariga Hitoshi; born August 23, 1972) is a professional artist who primarily illustrates manga and picture books, and has assumed the position of graphic designer for several Japanese titles in the game industry. He first began providing illustrations for the Pokémon Trading Card Game in 2011, though has been a fan of the franchise for many years. His main passion, however, lies with the franchise, known as Rockman in Japan, where he has illustrated numerous manga and artwork for affiliated products since the mid-90s. He likes to engage the community when he has the opportunity, appearing at exhibitions, and maintaining an online presence across several sites.

Ken Sugimori recognized Ariga's design work and invited him to work on X and Y. When designing Amaura and Aurorus, Ariga considered that a sauropod would pair well with Tyrunt and Tyrantrum, suggesting that the latter may have been considered first. Previous Pokémon such as Lapras, Meganium, and Deino already existed with a similar body shape, so Ariga chose to base the new family off the Amargasaurus, with the large fins on its neck. In creating the artwork for the villainous organization 3DS themes, Ariga pointed out the special attention given to how it looped seamlessly as the user navigated the 3DS menu. In the same thread, he also revealed that there were plans to create a 3DS theme for Team Flare, but they fell through as a result of the series moving from the 3DS to the Switch. Ariga's first spot as the lead character designer on the series was with Pokémon UNITE, though his affinity for paleontology led him to create a new design for Pikachu for the real-life Pokémon Fossil Museum, where he was reached out to by the organizers of the museum themselves.

Although he began officially working on the series in 2011 with the , his Pokémon fan art on DeviantArt dates back to 2010. From as early as 2011, Ariga would upload online battles against other players to his YouTube channel, which was something that he continued with well after the release of Sword and Shield. Though they were uploaded to what was originally his main YouTube channel, Ariga has since shifted focus to regularly live streaming art with his VTuber avatar.

name: James Turner
description:
James Turner, born 1978, is a British people graphic designer who works at The Pokémon Company International as a Creative Director of Pokémon Art and Design. Before this, he worked at Game Freak, during which he became the first Westerner to officially design Pokémon.

Turner designed Pokémon for Black and White, X and Y, Sun and Moon, Ultra Sun and Ultra Moon, and Sword and Shield; he was also the Art Director for the latter. Additionally, he directed the 2012 Nintendo 3DS eShop title HarmoKnight and the 2015 video game published by Sega, Tembo the Badass Elephant.

Before joining Game Freak, James Turner worked for eight years at Genius Sonority, and was credited under the name Jamie Turner (Japanese: ジェイミー・ターナー). The first game he worked on at this company was Pokémon Colosseum, for which Turner was responsible for the game's battle effects, battle camera, and cutscenes. For Pokémon XD: Gale of Darkness, Turner finalized Shadow Lugia based on various initial sketches of the design drawn by Hiromoto-SIN-ichi, which began after the conceptualization of the core game. He would then leave Genius Sonority to apply for another job, landing a position at GAME FREAK before the release of Pokémon Black and White. This was a change that he had decided upon during the pre-production phase of Pokémon Scarlet and Violet, shortly following the end of Sword and Shield's development.

On August 24, 2026, Turner announced that he had joined The Pokémon Company International as a Creative Director of Pokémon Art and Design.

name: Kagemaru Himeno
description:
Kagemaru Himeno (Japanese: 姫野かげまる), born July 24, 1972 in Kanagawa Prefecture, is a writer and illustrator who has provided material for Pokémon since the early years of the franchise. She started doing manga illustrations for RIBON Original in 1994, a magazine published by Shueisha, who along with other publishers Hakusensh and Shogakukan, own VIZ Media, which publishes manga outside Japan. Since 1997, Himeno has done many illustrations for Pokémon-related publications, including Pokémon Tales and her own series How I Became a Pokémon Card. She is also one of the few illustrators that has continued to produce card art since the early years of the Pokémon Trading Card Game. She likes to go by the nickname "Himemaru" (ヒメマル).

Himeno's artwork has been featured on cards since the Jungle expansion, and as such, it is usually instantly recognizable to long-time followers of the TCG. She openly admits that she loves the paintings she does, which reflects in the quality of her art. Himeno uses watercolors and often uses bright and vivid colors with softer tones to highlight areas of light and shadow. She also adds soft white flecks on some her images, which could be interpreted as cotton spores or the like. These are particularly apparent on her older works. Over the years, she has developed a sharper eye for detail, resulting in more crisp images with more adventurous backgrounds.

name: kawayoo
description:
Kawaguchi Yoohei (Japanese: 川口洋平), born 1974, is a freelance digital illustrator who has provided artwork for the Pokémon series. He began work with the Pokémon Trading Card Game, illustrating the Walrein (Rising Rivals 36), Hippopotas (Rising Rivals 64), and Nidorino (Rising Rivals 74) included in the Rising Rivals expansion. He is often credited by his nickname "kawayoo" (川洋) in his work.

Youhei's style is very distinctive, brought about from his creative approach and dedication to each one of his illustrations. He creates subjects from scratch by using a graphic tablet in image editing software and applying hundreds of strokes to define base shapes, outlines, backgrounds and final details. These result in often surreal, heavy, multi-layered images reminiscent of oil paintings. His images often focus on muscle tone, expression or contrast and have themes influenced by cyberpunk or anime. The Pokémon he has portrayed are often very detailed, vibrant and in dynamic positions, among which include the Pokémon C cards, which he provided all the artwork for (with the exception of LV.X variants). 

Youhei drew the promotional artwork, which includes booster pack art and theme deck art, for every expansion in the HeartGold & SoulSilver series. Outside the TCG, he illustrated maps and other promotional artwork for Pokémon Omega Ruby and Alpha Sapphire and every Generation VII core series game.

name: Keiji Kinebuchi
description:
Keiji Kinebuchi (Japanese: 杵淵敬二; born February 14, 1956 – c.2002) was a 3D illustrator who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game. When the TCG was first released, Kinebuchi was one of the few 3D artists, making his art for the first few expansions instantly recognizable. 

He designed his artwork using LightWave 3D.

Kinebuchi's last illustrations were featured in the Aquapolis expansion, during which time other 3D illustrators were beginning to contribute with more sophisticated images. He was credited as the illustrator for all Basic Energy cards, as well as a few Special Energy cards up until the Expedition Base Set, where there was a major change in the card layout. Mitsuhiro Arita designed the Energy symbols on the cards, whereas Kinebuchi designed the Energy cards' layouts.

Kinebuchi is also credited as an illustrator for some of the Trainer cards in the Pokémon Trading Figure Game; however, all of the images are taken from work he had previously done for the TCG.

Her debut work, Fukuyama Jikkuvukku, was self-published in 1981. Fukuyama's style involves the use of traditional mediums, including felt pens and pencils to create vibrant, colorful images. She has written and illustrated a handful of Pokémon-related books, and also provided a number of illustrations for the Pokémon Trading Card Game in 1999 and 2002, most notably Pokémon featured in the Rainbow Island aspect of the Southern Islands Collection.

name: Ken Sugimori
description:
Ken Sugimori (Japanese: 杉森建 Sugimori Ken; born January 27, 1966) is a friend of Satoshi Tajiri and illustrator of the original artwork for Pokémon games. He also has developed conceptual artwork for the movies, and illustrates cards and merchandising.

The original artwork for all 151 Generation I Pokémon was done by Ken Sugimori. In Red and Green, the in-game sprites were initially drawn by various artists. Sugimori later redrew each Pokémon in watercolor for promotional use. While doing so, he revised and refined many elements, which ultimately shaped how the designs were perceived by the public, with potential examples being Pikachu, Vaporeon, Dragonite, and Mew.

Sugimori's change of style over the years has been noticeable. Initially, he used a stiff, lightly shaded style using watercolors that was very reminiscent of Akira Toriyama's visual style, particularly that from 1989 onward. However, his now digitally-produced drawings of people and creatures have gradually gained more muscle definition, significantly rounder corners, heavier shading, and more natural and fluid poses.

Masago earned a bachelor's degree majoring in physics at Chuo University in 1983, and became a freelance artist in 1989. His first work, a manga series entitled Clown with Blue Nose, was first published in 1990. He has since gone on to produce many illustrations for numerous publications, even branching into the film industry in 2005, where he became a costume designer for the Chinese film The Promise. Masago provided illustrations for the Pokémon Trading Card Game between 2000 and 2005, depicting a number of Pokémon in a similar fashion to his traditional work, focusing on tone, areas of extreme color, and atmospheric environments.

name: Mana Ibe
description:
Mana Ibe (Japanese: 井部真那, born November 27, 1985 in Tokyo) is a graphic designer who has worked for the Pokémon Trading Card Game and video game series.

Ibe's first known involvement with the Pokémon franchise was in the staff of Pokémon Platinum under "Special Thanks", although it is currently unknown exactly what role she played in the development of that game. She later illustrated a card in the Arceus expansion: Manectric (Arceus 22). In the staff of Pokémon Black and White, she is listed under "Pokémon Designer". This is a résumé shared by Keiko Moritsugu and Reiko Tanoue, who both illustrated a single card from the Arceus expansion and are listed under the same roles in both sets of credits.

Ibe appears to have acquired a bigger role in Pokémon games since Black and White. In a interview with Junichi Masuda, it was revealed that she designed Victini. Along with Victini, she designed about 10 other Pokémon for Pokémon Black and White.

As of 2022, Ibe was appointed the art director of Pokémon Scarlet and Violet, her most senior role on the series thus far.

name: Masakazu Fukuda
description:
Masakazu Fukuda (Japanese: 福田正和) is an illustrator who was primarily involved with character and graphic design with many game companies in the 1990s before becoming a freelance illustrator. He has been providing artwork for the Pokémon Trading Card Game since 2003. 
Fukuda holds many artists in high regard and has several interests. He is a fan of mecha and admires the work of designer Hajime Katoki. Other favorites include manga artists Katsuhiro Otomo, Masamune Shirow and Akira Toriyama, as well as illustrators Jun Suemi and Takani Yoshiyuki, who designed the package art for many military model kits in the 1960s. He is a keen biker, engages in wide-angle photography, and enjoys electronic music and music from the late 60s, particularly that of James Brown.

name: match
description:
match is a Japanese digital illustrator who began providing artwork for the Pokémon Trading Card Game in 2009, with their first illustrations debuting in the HeartGold & SoulSilver expansion. Like similar digital artists, match applies many strokes utilizing a graphics tablet in image editing software to create their images.

match uses pattern brushes in select areas to achieve the desired texture in some illustrations, and often uses a subtle color palette combined with emphasis on light and shadow to help define the main subject, frequently accompanied by a prominent outline. In some cases, this technique gives an illusion of a 3D rendered model. In addition to providing artwork for the Pokémon TCG, match also began providing art for the Dimension-Zero TCG in 2010.

name: Mizue
description:
Mizue (Japanese: 瑞絵, Rui Zhao mizue) is a freelance illustrator and manga artist who has contributed artwork for the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Her first cards were Snubbull (Call of Legends 71) and Granbull (Call of Legends 26) from the Call of Legends expansion.

Many of her subjects are portrayed in dynamic poses, and colored using soft palettes and gradients with a definitive outline. The backgrounds of her artwork are more adventurous, particularly those that feature foliage, with individual leaves and plants incorporated into various gradient layers complete with a combination of halftone dots and horizontal lines. The majority of her subjects often include a white glow to help them stand out from the background. Bubbles and sparkles using lens flare also feature in many of her illustrations.

While she engages in producing personal drawings and comic strips, the majority of her professional work involves providing art for the Pokémon Trading Card Game.

Naoki Saito (Japanese: さいとうなおき Saitō Naoki, real name in kanji 齋藤直葵, born 1982 in Yamagata Prefecture, Japan) is a digital illustrator who has provided art for the Pokémon Trading Card Game since the HeartGold & SoulSilver expansion, as well as art for a couple of Pokémon games. Saito is a graduate of Tama Art University and previously worked at Konami Digital Entertainment Co., Ltd. before becoming freelance. In addition to the Pokémon TCG, he has also provided illustrations for several other trading card franchises: Juushinden: Ultimate Beast Battlers, and Eternal Wheel. 

Saito's style is vibrant and surreal, and often juxtaposes or merges the organic with the geometric. He also puts emphasis on texture to give subjects character. His work within the TCG is similar but subtler, instead using highlights and contrasting colors to make Pokémon stand out. In addition to card illustrations, Saito provided the packaging art for the Garchomp and Hydreigon Half Decks and the box art for Everyone's Exciting Battle. He also illustrated the Pokémon Tales book Crustle's Moving, available to read on the Pokémon Daisuki Club website.

name: Naoyo Kimura
description:
Naoyo Kimura (Japanese: Kimura Naoyo; born 1960) is an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Her first cards were Seel (Vending S2), Zapdos (Vending S2), and Graveler (Vending S2) from the Japanese Expansion Sheet Series 2. Her first cards released in English were the Wizards Black Star Promos Articuno (Wizards Promo 22), Zapdos (Wizards Promo 23), and Moltres (Wizards Promo 21) released alongside The Power of One. She is notable for creating illustrations for the Neo Series and the Southern Islands promotional set.

Besides contributing artwork for the Pokémon TCG, Naoyo Kimura illustrated multiple books from Pokémon Tales picture book series including Come Out, Squirtle!, Seel to the Resuce!, Beroringa Licks Everything, Fly On, Butterfree, Dragonite's Christmas and Don't Laugh, Charizard. For the 2023 "Pokémon x Van Gogh" art collaboration, Kimura contributed illustrations of Pikachu and the evolutionary lines of Honchkrow and Corviknight, inspired by Vincent van Gogh's Self-Portrait with Grey Felt Hat and Wheatfield with Crows, respectively.

description:
OKACHEKE (Japanese: おかちぇけ Okacheke) is a freelance illustrator who has worked on the Pokémon series. He was a semifinalist in the Illustration contests, where he submitted an illustration of Slowpoke. He began contributing official artwork for the Pokémon Trading Card Game with Shuppet (Chilling Reign 62), Skwovet (Chilling Reign 127), and Ice Rider Calyrex V (Chilling Reign 164) from the Chilling Reign expansion. Four years after submitting his Slowpoke artwork to the Illustration Grand Prix, OKACHEKE would officially illustrate the Slowpoke (151 79) included in the 151 expansion.

In addition to his work for the TCG, OKACHEKE was a visual development artist for Pokémon: Twilight Wings, and worked on concept art and set design for Detective Pikachu & the Mystery of the Missing Flan, as well as The Adventures of Snorlax & Cubone.

His first card was Snorlax (Promo-A 49), one of the Promo-A promotional cards. He made his physical Pokémon Trading Card Game debut afterward with illustrations of the Scolipede line in the Black Bolt expansion.

okayamatakatoshi is a graduate of Kyoto Seika University. Outside Pokémon, he works caricatures and picture books.

name: PLANETA
description:
PLANETA (Japanese: プラネッタ) is a Japanese design studio founded by illustrator Hideaki Hakozaki in September 2011 that specializes in 3D computer generated imagery for consumer games and graphical production, such as illustrations. Hakozaki established the studio with the drive to employ a new generation of artists to create and engineer new methods of delivering digital content that people can play with. It is currently based in Hamamatsucho, Minato-ku, Tokyo and, as of April 2025, has 23 employees. Much of the studio's portfolio centers on package artwork for Gundam model kits and producing 3D models for numerous games across several platforms. Within the Pokémon franchise, PLANETA has contributed towards the development of titles in the Pokémon Mystery Dungeon series, produced key visuals for Pokémon GO, and produced artwork for the Pokémon Trading Card Game and for Trading Card Game Pocket.

PLANETA as a studio began illustrating cards from the Flashfire expansion. The studio is credited as PLANETA CG Works in TCG Pocket. Individual artists began to be credited separately from the Forbidden Light expansion. These include:
Kazuya Igarashi (credited as PLANETA Igarashi)
Yuta Otani (credited as PLANETA Otani)
Ryosuke Tsuji (credited as PLANETA Tsuji)
Ultimateinudog (credited as PLANETA Mochizuki)
PLANETA Hiiragi
PLANETA Yamashita
PLANETA Saito
PLANETA Mamiya

The studio also began producing booster pack art from the Japanese Plasma Gale expansion and has continued to do so throughout subsequent TCG Eras, going on to produce art for booster packs and Theme Decks released outside Asia beginning with the BREAKthrough expansion. PLANETA also produced key visuals for Japanese TCG events and other boxed products. With the official release of the TCG in Thailand and Indonesia, the studio was also commissioned to provide booster pack art for the first four localized sets.

name: rina
description:
Christie (Japanese: リナ Rina) is a Pokémon Trainer and a character of the day who appeared in Where Did You Go, Audino?. 

Christie helped Officer Jenny investigate the Audino disappearances after another Audino, with whom she was good friends, disappeared. She and Doyle would often argue on who would find the missing Audino first and would compete with one another using their Psychic Pokémon. She also had a hunch that the Audino were being manipulated by some sort of Psychic attack.

Christie would later be partnered up with Iris to watch after Mimi's Audino, on which they had put a tracking device. The Audino soon started acting strange, so Christie and Iris began following it, only to meet up with Officer Jenny, Cilan, Doyle, and again. Christie managed to slow one down with Gothita's Telekinesis.

Christie and the others soon found all of the missing Audino and discovered that they were being controlled by sound waves created by . She used Gothita to battle Jessie's Woobat. After the case was solved, Christie was eager to know if her Gothita helped out more than Doyle's Solosis. However, Officer Jenny informed the both of them that Ash's Roggenrola helped out the most, leaving them both disappointed.

name: Ryo Ueda
description:
Ryo Ueda (Japanese: 植田亮 Ueda Ryō) is a 3D illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Following the development of 3D software and the death of the game's original 3D artist Keiji Kinebuchi, Ryo Ueda became one of the TCG's prominent 3D artists. His first cards were Chansey ex (EX Ruby & Sapphire 96), Scyther ex (EX Ruby & Sapphire 102), and Sneasel ex (EX Ruby & Sapphire 103) from the EX Ruby & Sapphire expansion. He would go on to provide many illustrations for Trainer cards and high-rarity Pokémon such as Pokémon-ex, Pokémon LV.X, and Full Art Pokémon-EX. During the Sun & Moon and Sword & Shield Series, Ueda also contributed various gold etched Secret cards.

Many of the Pokémon he has portrayed are powerful variants within the game, therefore Ueda creates solid renders and plays with lighting and elemental image effects, such as fire or lightning to often give the Pokémon a dominant presence. For non-Pokémon card images, he usually creates the item or location in the foreground and develops an accompanying background or environment to fit the purpose.

description:

During her career with the TCG, she began working as a character designer on Sun and Moon and Sword and Shield, where she created many of the games' various Pokémon Traineres. She draws digitally, opting to use Adobe Photoshop as her application of choice. 

Sakuma states that she began drawing from an early age with a particular interest in anime and manga, and was head of a manga club while at high school and college. She specializes in producing artwork with cute characters and invoking a warm atmosphere, utilizing a specific color palette and soft drawing style. She also experiments with different styles, including anime, impasto, and watercolor, and likes to convey a sense of motion in images that require it.

name: Shin Nagasawa
description:
Shin Nagasawa (Japanese: ) is a freelance illustrator who provides artwork for the Pokémon Trading Card Game and other Pokémon related merchandise. Nagasawa worked as a graphic designer at Square for a number of years after graduating from university in 1994, and was credited as a monster concept artist for several titles during this time. He went freelance in 2000, and has had numerous illustrations and manga series published since, as well as continuing to provide concept art for several games and illustrations for various trading card games. He often uses the pseudonym "JASON" (ジェイソン) or "J-mura" (J村) for self-published works (dōjinshi).

Nagasawa's first illustrations were featured Dragonite FB (Supreme Victors 56) and Regigigas FB (Supreme Victors 9) from the Supreme Victors expansion. In addition to card art, he has also produced the packaging artwork for expansions released outside of Japan, which include Boundaries Crossed, Plasma Storm, Plasma Freeze, and Plasma Blast. Other Pokémon related illustrations include those featured on merchandise sold in Japan. These include: Reshiram & Zekrom 2011 New Year's Greeting card and Pochi bags, Tepig, Pignite, and Emboar Uniqlo T-shirt design, Kyurem VS Tornadus•Thundurus•Landorus Pokémon Center stationery, and Gardevoir & Lilligant deck shields.

Nagasawa's illustration style within the TCG varies as does his work for other publications. Some are drawn in a style reminiscent of comic books, in that the Pokémon is drawn with a solid black outline, with areas of extreme shadow and other details also in solid black. In other illustrations, color shading is used to define details and the accompanying background, making outlines less explicit. In nearly all instances Nagasawa focuses on motion and a specific portion of the Pokémon's body with varying degrees of tilt, giving the impression that the Pokémon is moving out of the confines of the image.

name: Shinji Higuchi
description:
Shinji Higuchi (Japanese: 樋口真嗣), born September 22, 1965, Tokyo, is a writer, director, storyboard artist and a prominent special effects figure in Japanese film and television. As a teenager he was one of the four founding members of Gainax (originally established as Daicon Films), working on many anime and tokusatsu productions. He played an important part in the creation of the popular anime series , serving as writer, assistant director, and art director/storyboarder. His previous work on the anime led the show's director and fellow Gainax member Hideaki Anno to name Evangelion's protagonist, Shinji Ikari after him as an inside joke.

Higuchi initially started his career in the mid 80s working within special effects on several kaiju films, and by the mid 90's had established himself as a master within the field with the release of the acclaimed Gamera trilogy of films. During this time, he continued to be a storyboard artist for anime such as and , with his wife Noriko Takaya providing the namesake for the former's heroine. In addition to his special effects direction, Higuchi branched into CG animation for several tokusatsu films in the early 2000s, and has since directed a number of live-action films.

Higuchi became involved within the Pokémon franchise during the production of Jirachi: Wish Maker as a storyboard artist in 2004. He was later commissioned to produce the artwork for the new Pokémon LEGEND cards that first appeared in the HeartGold & SoulSilver expansion of the Pokémon Trading Card Game, and went on to co-illustrate all subsequent Pokémon LEGEND cards released in the HeartGold & SoulSilver Series. He was also involved in the art direction of two cards from the Undaunted expansion in collaboration with 3D illustrators Kent Kanetsuna and Wataru Kawahara, and remains the only person with a director credit on individual cards. In an interview with Tsunekazu Ishihara, Higuchi stated that his illustrations aim to depict Pokémon as realistic and monstrous.

name: Shinji Kanda
description:
Shinji Kanda (Japanese: カンダシンジ Kanda Shinji, born 1986 in Kyoto Prefecture) is an illustrator who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game.

Kanda's artworks are primarily done digitally, although he has used other artistic methods. For his first card, Magmar (Brilliant Stars 19) from the Brilliant Stars expansion, he used a technique of coloring on a plastic sheet using colored pencils before applying heat to shrink the plastic and enhance the colors. Kanda has also used various materials for his artworks, such as crumpled aluminum foil that he scanned for the artwork of SVP Promo Magneton (SVP Promo 159).

name: sui
description:
sui (Japanese: 彗) is a freelance digital illustrator who provides original illustrations for the Pokémon Trading Card Game, with her work debuting in the Arceus expansion. She has also produced an array of illustrations featured in a number of publications, such as guidebooks and CD covers. Sui specializes in depicting fantasy-scenes and animals, and includes animals and gaming among her interests. She particularly likes producing images that have a sense of motion. Sui also indulges in fan-art, which feature characters from many established Nintendo franchises.

sui uses a graphics tablet and a number of image editing software suites for her illustrations, which are created in an airbrush style. She uses areas of highly saturated color and luminosity in her work, resulting in vibrant, atmospheric, and serene images. Light is emphasized in almost all of her original work. Environments often incorporate elements of nature, as well as animals.

name: Taiga Kasai
description:
Taiga Kasai (Japanese: カサイタイガ Kasai Taiga) is an artist for the Pokémon series. He was a participant in both the Illustration contests and the Illustration contests illustration contests, being the Japanese First Runner-up for the latter. According to Kasai, he begged his parents to buy him the tools to allow him to enter, as being an artist on the TCG had always been a dream of his. Kasai's runner-up artwork would be used to create his first Pokémon card, Greninja (SWSH Promo 305), one of the SWSH Black Star Promos. When illustrating this artwork of Greninja, he carefully considered the contest's theme of how Pokémon would spend their days in the wild; seeing as Greninja is based on a ninja, he drew it as if it was planning a strategy for battle. 

Kasai also confirmed that he drew many drafts for each individual Pokémon that was eligible for the contest, though he knew his idea for Greninja was the perfect fit from the very start. That being said, Kasai admitted he struggled with the background of the piece, saying that his leading concern was making the subject stand out from the background itself. It didn't start to sink in that he had won the award until he had received the physical copy of the Greninja card, and seeing the existing TCG artists that he looked up to congratulate him on Twitter after announcing that he had won the award was a huge moment for him. He draws digitally, opting to use an iPad Pro.

He first began drawing after seeing a Pokémon illustration by his father, who was already an artist. He didn't think of himself as particularly good, though decided to go to art school when taking the entrance exams for university, which was where he began studying how to draw. Though Kasai first learned about Pokémon when he was in kindergarten through the stickers found on the series' branded Daiichi Pan, the first game he played was Pokémon Ruby and Sapphire, which also happen to be his favorites. He first discovered the Pokémon Trading Card Game when sets were on sale at the theater when Kasai first watched M05, with his long-standing appeal for the game being as a result of its wealth of unique and talented illustrators.

In 2023, he made his debut as a game artist on Pokémon HOME and Pokémon GO. Kasai's favorite Pokémon is Aggron.

Born in Germany, Terada Tera lived there for ten years before moving to Japan. She uses pop art style and distinctive colors in her work. She is well-known for illustrating music videos, such as Akari Nanawo's Turing Love feat.Sou, Ado (singer)'s Ashura-chan, and a host of Vocaloid credits. She has also worked with the Hello Kitty brand for the series' 50th anniversary.

name: Tetsuo Hara
description:
Tetsuo Hara (Japanese: 原 哲夫 Hara Tetsuo; born September 2, 1961) is a Japanese manga artist and illustrator who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Hara is best known as the co-creator and illustrator of the manga with writer Buronson; it is one of the best-selling manga in history, with over 100 million copies sold. Hara has also illustrated the manga and the Fist of the North Star prequel .

For the Palafin ex illustration, Hara stated that he aimed to add his own appeal of "coolness", which he is particular about, to the card art while maintaining the Pokémon style. He paid special attention to the reflections of the light and the water, and created the appearance of Palafin's fists leaving afterimages. The main fists are given red coloring to make them stand out.

name: The Pokémon Company Art Team
description:
The Pokémon Company ( Pokémon) is a company responsible for the licensing and marketing of the Pokémon franchise. Founded on April 23, 1998 with the name The Pokémon Center Company ( Pokémon Center kabushiki gaisha) as a joint venture by Nintendo, Game Freak, and Creatures, it was created to manage the Pokémon Center stores in Japan. It has since expanded to be responsible for the games, Trading Card Game, license management, animation and movie, and other ancillary businesses in Japan and Asia. Its wholly owned subsidiaries, Pokémon Korea, Inc. and The Pokémon Company International, manage these responsibilities in South Korea and areas outside Asia, respectively. In March 2024, The Pokémon Company and ILCA established The Pokémon Works as a joint venture.

As of March 31, 2025, The Pokémon Company has shipped over 489 million units of their video games and over 75 billion trading cards. Tsunekazu Ishihara is the President and CEO of the company.

description:
Tokiya Sakuba (Japanese: 作場季野), often credited as simply TOKIYA (トキヤ), is a freelance digital illustrator who has provided art for the Pokémon Trading Card Game since the Arceus expansion. She was born in 1983 in Tokyo, Japan.

Her style is very similar to that of kawayoo, utilizing a graphic tablet in image editing software to create base outlines, shapes and final details culminating in complex and atmospheric images. Her art focuses on insects, mechanics and the human body resulting in often very surreal images – some of which are quite extreme compared to similar artists, featuring elements of nudity and graphic violence. The Pokémon she has portrayed, as well as their environment, are very detailed and have surreal qualities.

name: Tomohiro Kitakaze
description:
Tomohiro Kitakaze (Japanese: 北風友裕, born April 8th, 1983 in Kobe) is a freelance illustrator. He is an Osaka University of Arts graduate and previously worked at Monolith Soft as a 2D designer, providing concept art for characters, monsters, and machinery. He later worked for Game Freak, again as a 2D designer, providing concept art and designs for Pokémon characters, though it is unknown how many Pokémon he has designed.

In addition, he also provided artwork for one card from the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Kitakaze's subjects are initially drawn traditionally, and then enhanced digitally afterwards. His cartoon strips and characters are created in anime style, though his more detailed illustration work draws inspiration from mythical creatures and the occult, sometimes incorporating mechanical motifs. 

He claims that his design for Mewtwo was influenced by his adoration for Mewtwo Strikes Back as a child.

name: Tomokazu Komiya
description:
Tomokazu Komiya (Japanese: こみやトモカズ Komiya Tomokazu; born 1973) is an illustrator who has provided art for the Pokémon Trading Card Game, as well as several Pokémon Tales books. His illustration style is well known within the Pokémon community particularly due to his deformed and loosely colored images. This is intentional, as Komiya is a practitioner of Primitivism, an art movement that takes inspiration from themes or stylistic elements of prehistory, tribal cultures, or children's art.

For the 2023 "Pokémon x Van Gogh" art collaboration, Komiya contributed illustrations of Sunflora and Smeargle, inspired by Vincent van Gogh's Sunflowers and Self-Portrait as a Painter, respectively.

Then, after a nearly 19 year absence, Toshinao Aoki returned to the TCG to illustrate Exeggutor (Crown Zenith 58) for Crown Zenith, and has once again become a recurring illustrator.

In addition to Pokémon cards, his artwork was featured in the Pokémon Tales story books Pikachu's Day, Lapras Makes a Friend, I'm Not Pikachu, and Wake Up, Lugia!.

Toyste Beach (Japanese: トイストビーチ Toyste Beach) is a game and video development studio that has contributed illustrations for the Pokémon Trading Card Game. Its first artworks were Celebi-EX (Boundaries Crossed 9), Keldeo-EX (Boundaries Crossed 49), and Town Map (Boundaries Crossed 136) from the Boundaries Crossed expansion, although the BW Black Star Promos Mewtwo-EX (BW Promo 45) and Darkrai-EX (BW Promo 46) released beforehand internationally. The studio is mostly known for illustrating Trainer cards, but it has also illustrated a small number of Pokémon cards. Its artists have been known to illustrate both 3D CG and 2D on drawing programs.

name: Tsuyoshi Nagano
description:
Tsuyoshi Nagano (Japanese: 長野剛 Nagano Tsuyoshi; born 1961) is an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game. His first card was Haxorus (Shrouded Fable 46) from the Shrouded Fable expansion.

Nagano is a member of the Tokyo Illustrators Society, and is most famously known for cover artwork for the , , and video game series by Koei since the 1980s. He has also worked for Lucasfilm, having created artwork and illustrations for the franchise.

name: Ultimateinudog
description:
Ultimateinudog (born December 3, 1997), formerly credited under the name PLANETA Mochizuki, is an illustrator who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game. The first card they illustrated was Gardevoir V (Champion's Path 70) from the Japanese Explosive Walker expansion, and their first cards released in English were Mew V (Darkness Ablaze 69) and Crobat V (Darkness Ablaze 104) from the Darkness Ablaze expansion. Their first card credited as Ultimateinudog was Mandibuzz ex (Ascended Heroes 139) from the Ascended Heroes special expansion.

Ultimateinudog is a former illustrator at PLANETA. They left the company and went freelance on July 31, 2024.

The entirety of Ultimateinudog's work on the TCG has been 3D renders used for Rule Box Pokémon or Full Art cards. They have also illustrated banners for Ranked Battle regulations in Scarlet & Violet's Battle Stadium.

name: Uninori
description:
Uninori (Japanese: 雲丹海苔) is an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game, their first work being published in 2024 with Grotle (Temporal Forces 11) from the Temporal Forces expansion. As early as 2018, Uninori submitted various pieces to Pokémon's TCG Illustration Contests.

Judging from posts on social media, Uninori is heavily inspired by a variety of artists, namely Pokémon's Ken Sugimori and Kagemaru Himeno, as well as and artist Akira Toriyama. This inspiration is further reflected in their style for the TCG, which was described in a Pokémon.com article as evoking the art style of the manga and anime industries during the 1990s.

Uninori's favorite Trainer battle theme is from Johto.

name: USGMEN
description:
USGMEN (Japanese: うさぎメン Usagi-men) is a Japanese freelance artist for the Pokémon series, beginning as an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game. His first card was Mew ex (Paldean Fates 232) from the Paldean Fates expansion.

In 2024, he was a key animator on the Pokémon Day 2024 video POKÉDANCE, and also designed the character dancing with the Hoenn first partner Pokémon. He also frequently posts animated Pokémon fan-art on his Twitter.

name: Yamazaki Rei
description:
Rei Yamazaki (Japanese: 山崎玲愛 Yamazaki Rei) is an animator, illustrator, and character designer who has worked on the Pokémon series. She is one of the chief animation directors and the lead character designer for HZ.

Yamazaki began working on the Pokémon series as a key animator for XY. She made her animation directorial debut on Rise and Shine, Starship! during SM. In addition to her work on the main Pokémon animated series, she also directed the first episode of Pokémon Evolutions, The Champion.

She is credited as Yamazaki Rei as an illustrator for the Trading Card Game. She illustrates exclusively for cards related to the animated series. Her first cards were the SVP Black Star Promos Sprigatito (SVP Promo 191) and Terapagos & Friends (SVP Promo).

name: Yano Keiji
description:
Yano Keiji (Japanese: 矢野恵司 Yano Keiji; born 1988 in the Kōchi Prefecture) is a freelance illustrator who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game. His first card was Comfey (Crown Zenith GG14) from the Crown Zenith expansion.

Yano's artistic influences include Japanese and artstyles, Buddhist statues, and the works of 20th-century Western painting Pablo Picasso, Paul Cézanne, and Giorgio de Chirico. He is a graduate of Tokyo University of the Arts, where he studied sculpture. Prior to his work on the Pokémon series, he worked as a 3D illustrator for four years at Nintendo, and went freelance in 2017.

Yano was a fan of Gold and Silver, the Pokémon animated series, and the Pokémon Trading Card Game as a child, and continues to play the TCG and Pokémon GO as an adult.

name: Yasuda Shuhei
description:
Shūhei Yasuda (Japanese: Yasuda Shūhei) is a character designer, animation director and key animator of the animated series.

Yasuda began working on the animated series as a key animator during XY, with his first credit being for the ending animation of DreamDream. He was promoted to a character designer on SM, then held the position of chief animation director for JN. He also animation-directed the opening animations for the all versions of One, Two, Three.

Additionally, Yasuda has contributed illustrations for the Trading Card Game, exclusively for cards related to the animated series.

name: YOSHIROTTEN
description:
Yoshi Nishi (born 1983), also known as YOSHIROTTEN (Japanese: ヨシロットン) is a Tokyo-based graphic artist and art director who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game.

YOSHIROTTEN debuted as a Pokémon TCG artist with the 30th Celebration special expansion, of which he is responsible for the set's key visual. YOSHIROTTEN illustrated Futuristic rare cards, RGB rare cards, and Futuristic rare-style Basic Energy cards introduced in the expansion.

YOSHIROTTEN's artworks are futuristic and abstract, presenting a science fiction theme based on fundamental concepts such as color, the Earth, the Sun, and so on. Selected exhibitions include "FUTURE NATURE" (2018), "SUN" (2023), "Radial Graphics Bio" (2024), and "FUTURE NATURE II" (2024). He runs his own creative studio YAR, funded in 2015. He collaborated with companies such as Hermès, McLaren and NIKE.

name: Yukihiro Tada
description:
Yukihiro Tada (Japanese: タダユキヒロ Tada Yukihiro; born in Osaka) is a freelance illustrator and comic artist who has contributed artwork for the Pokémon Trading Card Game. His first card was illustration rare Pinsir (Twilight Masquerade 168) from the Twilight Masquerade expansion.

Yukihiro Tada graduated from the faculty of arts at Kyoto Seika University. He won the annual prize in The Choice held in 2005 by Genkosha, a publishing company, and also created illustrations for the official Japanese lyric video for , a song by Lukas Graham nominated for three Grammys.

His illustrations for the TCG typically involve laidback environmental scenes.

name: Yusuke Ohmura
description:
Yusuke Ohmura (Japanese: 大村祐介 Ōmura Yūsuke, born July 6, 1981) is an illustrator of the artwork for Pokémon games since Diamond and Pearl. He has drawn several characters for the core series games starting with Black and White, such as Gym Leaders and the Elite Four of Unova.

Ohmura created the designs for Piplup, Oshawott, and the game mascots of Pokémon X and Y, Xerneas and Yveltal. Initial design for the two Legendary Pokémon was started by Ken Sugimori, but after he encountered '', he gave the work to Ohmura, who furthered the designs. Sugimori later returned to finish them. In Pokémon Sun and Moon, he became the lead of Pokémon designer, switching his role with Sugimori.

In 2016, Ohmura left Game Freak and became a freelance illustrator.

He is also an illustrator for the Pokémon Trading Card Game, starting with the Mysterious Treasures expansion.

name: Yuu Nishida
description:
Yuu Nishida (Japanese: 西田ユウ Nishida Yuu) is a freelance illustrator who has contributed artwork to the Pokémon Trading Card Game since winning the Illustration contests. Nishida's submitted illustration would be used as the art for her first card, Gardevoir (SM-P Promo 408), one of the SM-P Promotional cards. Beginning with Celebi (Shining Fates 3) from Shining Fates, Nishida has been illustrating cards on a regular basis. She also illustrated the booster pack artwork for VMAX Climax.

Nishida has been drawing every day since she was young. She began illustrating professionally in 2017, and works part-time as an art teacher at the high school she attended in her youth. She currently uses a touchscreen tablet and Clip Studio Paint to produce her artwork. Nishida became a fan of the Pokémon franchise as a child, playing Pokémon FireRed and watching Jirachi: Wish Maker. Nishida's favorite generation is Generation V, and her favorite Pokémon is Yamask.
